summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Pentair picks up ex-Fiserv CFO
articles.description: Former Fiserv CFO Bob Hau is stepping into Pentair’s top finance seat as it seeks to close a $1.4 billion acquisition of Taco Group.

articles.title: How digital IDs may battle fraud
articles.description: Americans are vulnerable to identification and payment frauds because the U.S. has been slow to adopt digital identification, two Congress members contend.

articles.title: Amazon blocks Meta’s AI shopper
articles.description: The e-commerce giant said Meta had failed to notify it about the Muse agent accessing its retail site to make purchases on behalf of consumers.

articles.title: Adyen snaps up Klarna CFO
articles.description: The Dutch digital payments processor has hired Niclas Neglen as its new chief financial officer, but he won’t join until next year.

articles.title: PayCompass, Simpay and Exectras come together
articles.description: The three payments companies have formed a new processing venture that also sells healthcare services to merchants.

articles.title: Merchants call card-fee pact unconstitutional
articles.description: Walmart and other retailers argue that forcing them to stay in a swipe-fee settlement class violates their due process rights.

articles.title: Ramp tackles accounts receivable
articles.description: “Finance teams today spend too much time chasing payments for outstanding invoices,” Ramp’s chief product officer said.

articles.title: Cross-border contest heats up
articles.description: Technological innovation has enabled fintechs to carve out a beachhead in cross-border payments, but banks still have cards to play.
